_about: The single source of truth for this platform: what it accepts and what we have learned about it. Every skill, job and script that makes or posts videos for it reads this file; put new findings here, not anywhere else. maxSeconds is the platform's limit. A video longer than that never goes out cut: the video build makes a separate version for this platform of at most versionSeconds, with its own hook, payoff and end card (data.versions.<platform>), and the publisher posts it only when that version exists.

metadata.title: The YouTube title without " #shorts".
metadata.text: Like Instagram but without the @handle line and with at most 3 hashtags; Facebook reads it as a post, so the first line is a full sentence (it still holds the `search` phrase).

notes: Page Reels take 3 to 90 s (reelSeconds). A longer video goes up as a normal Page video (up to maxSeconds, 4 h): the publisher sends Facebook the same public link Instagram gets, and Social Media Publisher posts it through /{page-id}/videos. When the build made a Facebook version (data.versions.facebook), that Reel is posted instead, since Reels reach more people.
Posting times (IST) are the same 5 as Instagram (one publish run posts to every platform); see the reasoning in instagram.json. Page Reels have no daily cap that 5 posts comes near.

Cover (26 Nov 2026): the publisher sets the video's thumbnail (data.thumb) as the Reel's cover after upload, through Facebook's video thumbnails call. If Facebook refuses it, the Reel keeps a frame Facebook picks, so the first frame still matters.
